mainTopic: מודה בקנס ואחר כך באו עדים: רבן גמליאל's admission, the dispute of רב and שמואל, and when an admission exempts from a קנס
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רבן גמליאל, who blinded his slave טבי's eye and told רבי יהושע. The גמרא explains that he was not in a בית דין, so his admission did not count. Another version has רבי יהושע say 'you already admitted.' The גמרא explains that the two versions differ only on whether the talk happened in court, not on the law. Then רב and שמואל argue about someone who admits to a קנס and afterward עדים come: רב says פטור, and שמואל says חייב. רב's proof from the פסוקים is turned aside by שמואל. A ברייתא about a thief who admits when he sees עדים coming forces שמואל to say he follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. רב can fit both תנאים, because a frightened admission is different from a free one. רב המנונא, backed by רבי יוחנן, limits רב's rule to an admission that makes the thief owe something, and רבא challenges this from the רבן גמליאל story. רב אשי begins to bring support from the wording of a משנה, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The admission was not made in court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question: רבי יהושע was not sitting as a court when רבן גמליאל told him, so the admission does not count as a legal admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי יהושע) was standing outside of a court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question asked just before this section. It explains that רבן גמליאל's admission did not count, because he did not say it in front of a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: רבן גמליאל admitted, so why would witnesses still make him free טבי, if admitting to a קנס exempts you? The answer is that only an admission made in a בית דין exempts you from a קנס. An admission made outside of court is legally treated as if it never happened, so witnesses could still obligate him.

keyTerms.meaning: not in a court; outside a formal court setting
was standing / was situated
a fine; a payment set by the תורה that is more than the actual damage, like freeing a slave

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of the discussion. It answers a question from the previous lines: why witnesses would matter after רבן גמליאל had already admitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea of the whole section: an admission only exempts you from a קנס if it is made in front of a בית דין.

phrases.english: He was standing not in a court.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע. Since this was not a court, רבן גמליאל's admission to him did not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין הֲוָה קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section, about why witnesses would matter after an admission.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: the admission happened outside of court, so it has no legal force.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבן גמליאל admitted, witnesses coming later should not obligate him, if admitting to a קנס exempts you.
steps.terutzMaskana: An admission outside of court is not a legal admission, so later witnesses could still obligate him.

steps.title: A different ברייתא: 'Because you already admitted'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהושע gives a different reason: the words mean nothing because רבן גמליאל already admitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: He (רבי יהושע) said to him: Your words mean nothing, because you already admitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of the same story. In this version, רבי יהושע's reason is that רבן גמליאל already admitted, not that he had no witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version suggests the admission did count, so even if witnesses came later, טבי would not go free. That clashes with the answer in step 1, which said the admission did not count because it was outside of court. Now there are two ברייתות that seem to say opposite things.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא (opens a challenge from a source)
your words mean nothing
you admitted

phrases.english: But it was taught: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע is speaking to רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: There is nothing in your words, because you already admitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין בִּדְבָרֶיךָ כְּלוּם, שֶׁכְּבָר הוֹדִיתָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 1 with a ברייתא that treats רבן גמליאל's admission as valid.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 1, that רבן גמליאל's admission did not count because it was outside of court.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהושע says 'you already admitted,' then the admission did count. That would mean the conversation was a real admission, against step 1.

steps.title: Suggestion: the two ברייתות are a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the two versions show a real dispute between תנאים about whether someone who admits to a קנס is obligated if witnesses come later.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, is it not a dispute between תנאים? This תנא, who says 'because you have no witnesses,' holds that one who admits to a קנס and then witnesses come is obligated. And this תנא, who says 'because you already admitted,' holds that one who admits to a קנס and then witnesses come is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to explain why the two ברייתות give different reasons. Maybe the two תנאים disagree about the basic law of מודה בקנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says 'you have no witnesses,' which hints that witnesses would still make him pay, even after he admitted. The second says 'you already admitted,' which hints that the admission exempts him for good. So the גמרא suggests a disagreement: one תנא says obligated, the other says exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: what, is it not...? (introduces a suggested explanation)
it is a dispute between תנאים
one who admits he owes a קנס
and afterward witnesses came

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. 'You have no witnesses' points to OBLIGATED once witnesses come. 'You already admitted' points to EXEMPT even if witnesses come.

phrases.english: What, is it not a dispute of תנאים?

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא דְּאָמַר ״שֶׁכְּבָר אֵין לְךָ עֵדִים״,
phrases.english: This תנא, who says 'because you have no witnesses,'
holds: one who admits to a fine
and afterward witnesses came, is obligated;
and this תנא, who says 'because you already admitted,'
holds: one who admits to a fine
and afterward witnesses came, is exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי, לָאו תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the conflict raised in step 2 by turning it into a dispute between תנאים about the law of מודה בקנס.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the two versions of רבי יהושע's words a dispute about whether witnesses can obligate someone who already admitted to a קנס?

steps.title: No: everyone agrees, they only disagree about whether it was in court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. All agree that admitting to a קנס exempts you even if witnesses come later. The two ברייתות only disagree about whether רבי יהושע was in court at the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that one who admits to a קנס and then witnesses come is exempt. What they disagree about is this: the תנא who says 'because you have no witnesses' holds that it was outside of court. The תנא who says 'because you already admitted' holds that it was in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says there is no dispute about the law at all. The two versions just tell the story differently: one has it outside of court, the other in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law is the same for everyone: a real admission to a קנס exempts you, even if witnesses come later. The first ברייתא says רבי יהושע was outside of court, so the admission did not count, and only the missing witnesses saved רבן גמליאל. The second says he was in court, so the admission counted and exempted him.

keyTerms.meaning: according to everyone; all agree
and about this they disagree
outside of court

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, both ברייתות agree: if you admit to a קנס in court, you are exempt even if witnesses come later. An admission outside of court does not count. The two ברייתות only disagree about the facts: was רבי יהושע in court or not?
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the רבן גמליאל story does not have to be a dispute about מודה בקנס, since both versions can hold that admission exempts. It also shows the rule only works when the admission is made in a בית דין.

phrases.english: No; everyone agrees:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה בִּקְנָס וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים – פָּטוּר;
phrases.english: one who admits to a fine and afterward witnesses came is exempt;
and about this they disagree:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא דְּאָמַר ״שֶׁכְּבָר אֵין לְךָ עֵדִים״,
phrases.english: this תנא, who says 'because you have no witnesses,'
holds: it was outside of court.
phrases.notes: So the admission did not count, and only the missing witnesses kept טבי from going free.

phrases.english: and that תנא, who says 'because you already admitted,'
holds: it was in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא, מוֹדֶה בִּקְנָס וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 3's suggestion of a dispute about the law, and moves the disagreement to the facts of the story.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the תנאים disagree about the law of מודה בקנס ואחר כך באו עדים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The different wordings can be explained by a disagreement about the facts (in court or outside of court), not about the law.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All agree that one who admits to a קנס in court is exempt even if witnesses come later. The two versions differ only about whether the conversation took place in a בית דין.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about admitting to a fine before witnesses come
steps.stepSummary: רב says one who admits to a קנס and later עדים come is פטור; שמואל says he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If someone admits that he owes a fine, and afterward witnesses come and testify, רב says he is exempt, and שמואל says he is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute between two אמוראים, רב and שמואל, about a person who admits to a קנס and then עדים show up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a person's own admission alone does not make him pay a קנס. The question here is what happens when real עדים come afterward. רב says the earlier admission already exempted him for good; שמואל says the עדים now make him pay.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces a teaching or dispute of the אמוראים
One who admits to a fine (a payment beyond the actual damage)
Exempt; does not have to pay
Obligated; must pay

steps.confusionAlert: Step 4 only showed that the two ברייתות about רבן גמליאל do not have to disagree on this law. Here two later אמוראים, רב and שמואל, argue about it openly. Later, in steps 12–13, the תנאים of another ברייתא turn out to argue about a related case.

phrases.english: It was stated: one who admits to a fine,
and afterward witnesses came —
Rav says: he is exempt,
and Shmuel says: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the explicit dispute of the אמוראים on the question that was raised and set aside in the תנאים discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: one who admits to a קנס and then עדים come is פטור. שמואל: he is חייב.

steps.title: רב's source from the doubled word 'found'
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר אהילאי explains that רב learns from 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' that the קנס of double payment needs both עדים and דיינים, which excludes someone who admits on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר אהילאי said: What is רב's reason? The פסוק says 'אִם הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא': 'if it is found' means through witnesses, and 'it shall be found' means through judges. This excludes a person who makes himself guilty by his own words.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר אהילאי gives the source for רב's view from the פסוק about a thief paying double.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah doubles the word 'found'. רב reads each word as a separate requirement: the theft must be found through עדים, and then found guilty by דיינים. A person who confesses on his own did not come through that process, so he is not charged the קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'Found, it shall be found': the doubled word in the פסוק about a thief
Judges
One who makes himself guilty, meaning he confesses on his own

phrases.english: Rava bar Ahilai said:
What is the reason of Rav?
"If it is found" — through witnesses,
phrases.notes: שמות 22:3. The פסוק doubles the word 'found', and רב learns something from each half.

phrases.english: "it shall be found" — through judges;
excluding one who incriminates himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for רב's ruling in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that self-admission prevents a קנס

steps.title: Why is this derivation needed if another verse already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this פסוק is needed, since 'אשר ירשיען' already teaches that self-admission does not create a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this? It already comes from the words 'אֲשֶׁר יַרְשִׁיעֻן', 'whom the judges convict'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the derivation by pointing out that a different פסוק already teaches the same rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אשר ירשיען' already means only a person the judges convict pays double, not someone who confesses. So the doubled 'found' would be extra. This question is not meant to knock down רב. It sets up a sharper proof for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? Asked when a teaching seems extra
'Whom the judges convict': another פסוק about double payment
It comes out from (another source)

phrases.english: Why do I need it?
It is derived from "whom the judges convict"!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי? מֵ״אֲשֶׁר יַרְשִׁיעֻן״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the derivation in step 6 is needed, leading to a refined proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' to exclude self-admission
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule is already taught by 'אשר ירשיען', so this פסוק would be extra if it taught only that.

steps.title: The extra verse proves admission exempts even when witnesses come later
steps.stepSummary: Since the basic rule is already known, the extra פסוק must teach that one who admits to a קנס stays פטור even when עדים come afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: one who admits to a fine, and afterward witnesses come, is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב's proof. The extra פסוק is used to teach the case of עדים coming after the admission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because 'אשר ירשיען' already covers simple self-admission, 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' must add something new. The new point is that once he admitted, he is exempt for good, even if עדים testify later. This is exactly רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: turns to the real explanation
Learn from this: draws a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: רב's proof works in two steps: one פסוק teaches that self-admission alone does not create a קנס, and the extra doubled פסוק teaches that the admission exempts him even if עדים come later.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה בִּקְנָס וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים –
phrases.english: one who admits to a fine and afterward witnesses came —
is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by giving the extra פסוק a new job, which completes רב's proof.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that admission exempts even when עדים come later
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא', since 'אשר ירשיען' already teaches the basic rule

steps.title: שמואל: 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' is needed for a different lesson
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' is needed to teach that the thief himself pays double, as דבי חזקיה taught. So only 'אשר ירשיען' teaches that self-admission does not create a קנס, and nothing is left over to prove רב's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל can say to you: That פסוק ('הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא') is needed to teach that the thief himself pays double, as the school of חזקיה taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by showing that the 'extra' פסוק is not extra at all. It teaches a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's proof depended on 'אשר ירשיען' already teaching that self-admission does not create a קנס, which made 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' extra. שמואל says 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' is busy teaching something else: that the thief himself pays double, as דבי חזקיה learned from it. So 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' is not extra, only 'אשר ירשיען' teaches the rule about self-admission, and שמואל can hold the person is חייב when עדים come later.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for (a different teaching)
The thief himself
A teaching from the school of חזקיה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common pattern in the גמרא: a proof built on an 'extra' word fails as soon as the other side shows the word is needed for something else.

phrases.english: And Shmuel can say to you:
That is needed for the thief himself,
phrases.notes: 'That' means 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא'. It teaches that the thief himself pays double.

phrases.english: as the school of Ḥizkiyya taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 8 by giving 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' a different job, so it is no longer extra. This defends שמואל's ruling from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' is extra and teaches רב's ruling. It still teaches the basic rule that self-admission alone does not create a קנס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא' is not extra. It is needed to teach that the thief himself pays double, as דבי חזקיה taught, so only 'אשר ירשיען' teaches the rule about self-admission.

steps.title: רב challenges שמואל from a thief who admits as witnesses approach
steps.stepSummary: רב brings a ברייתא: a thief who sees עדים coming and admits to stealing pays only קרן. This seems to say he stays פטור from the קנס even after the עדים come, which goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב objected to שמואל: If a thief saw witnesses coming toward him and said, 'I stole, but I did not slaughter or sell it,' he pays only the principal!
steps.whatsHappening: רב attacks שמואל with a ברייתא. In it, a thief admits right before the עדים arrive, and he pays only the value of what he stole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עדים were already on their way, so they would have testified after his admission. If he still pays only קרן, then admitting first protects him from the קנס even when עדים come later. That is רב's view and goes against שמואל, who says he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
Coming closer, on their way
The principal: just the value of what was stolen, with no extra fine
Slaughtering or selling the stolen animal, which brings the payment of ארבעה וחמשה

phrases.english: Rav raised an objection to Shmuel:
If he saw witnesses who were approaching,
phrases.notes: "He" is a thief. The witnesses are coming to testify against him.

phrases.english: and he said: "I stole,
but I did not slaughter and I did not sell" –
he pays only the principal!
phrases.notes: He pays no double payment and no four or five times payment, only what he took.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from a פסוק was turned away in step 9, רב now attacks שמואל directly from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one who admits to a קנס is חייב when עדים come later
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The עדים were about to testify, yet the thief pays only קרן. So an earlier admission keeps him פטור even with later עדים.

steps.title: שמואל: the witnesses turned back
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the עדים turned around and never testified. Only his own admission is left, and that cannot create a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to him: What case are we dealing with here? Where the witnesses turned back and left.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains the ברייתא as a narrow case. The עדים never actually testified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the עדים left, there is no testimony at all, only the thief's own admission. Everyone agrees an admission alone does not create a קנס. So the ברייתא says nothing about a case where עדים really do testify later.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to limit a source to a specific case
They turned back and did not testify

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here, with what are we dealing?
Such as where the witnesses went back.
phrases.notes: He means the witnesses never ended up testifying.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's challenge from step 10 by limiting the ברייתא to a narrow case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to mean the עדים testified after the admission and he was still פטור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עדים turned back, so only the admission remains, and that cannot create a קנס.

steps.title: רב: the end of the ברייתא shows the witnesses did testify
steps.stepSummary: רב points to the סיפא, where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says 'let the עדים come and testify.' That suggests the תנא קמא holds their testimony does not help, so the case must involve עדים who could testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says, 'Let the witnesses come and testify.' This shows that the first תנא holds: no, their testimony does not help!
steps.whatsHappening: רב rejects שמואל's answer by using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says the עדים should come and testify, so the case is one where they can testify. Since he is arguing with the תנא קמא, the תנא קמא must hold that even if they testify, the thief pays only קרן. That is exactly רב's view, and it means שמואל's 'they turned back' reading does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of a משנה or ברייתא
By inference, from what is implied
The first, unnamed תנא in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches,
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
Let the witnesses come and testify;
by inference, the first tanna holds: no!
phrases.notes: The "no" means their testimony would make no difference, and he pays only the principal anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects שמואל's answer from step 11 by reading it against the ברייתא's own סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the עדים turned back
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מחלוקת in the סיפא only makes sense if the עדים can testify. So the תנא קמא holds that later testimony does not create the קנס, against שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל: I hold like רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: שמואל concedes that the תנא קמא disagrees with him. He says his own ruling follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to him: Isn't there רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds like me? What I said follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל stops defending his reading and admits the תנא קמא of the ברייתא is against him. He relies on the other תנא in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A source from one תנא cannot overturn an אמורא who follows a different תנא. Since רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says the עדים should come and testify, the thief becomes חייב in the קנס, just as שמואל ruled. So the challenge is answered by placing שמואל on one side of a מחלוקת of תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: He stands with me, he holds like my view
What I said, my statement

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the תנא קמא agrees with him. He is admitting the תנא קמא disagrees and choosing the other side of the מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אִיכָּא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Isn't there Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
who stands in line with me?
What I said –
follows Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִיכָּא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּקָאֵי כְּווֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by giving up the narrow reading and relying on רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to be contradicted by the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the תנא קמא contradicts him. שמואל follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, which is a valid position.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the אמוראים' מחלוקת to a known מחלוקת of תנאים, and that sets up the next question about רב.

steps.title: Must רב's view also depend on the מחלוקת of תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that שמואל clearly depends on a מחלוקת of תנאים. It then asks whether רב's view must also depend on it, or whether רב can fit both תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to שמואל, it is certainly a מחלוקת of תנאים. According to רב, shall we say it is also a מחלוקת of תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks whether רב is stuck agreeing with only the תנא קמא, or whether רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון could also agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל openly admitted that he holds like one תנא only. The גמרא prefers not to tie an אמורא to just one side if it can be avoided. So it looks for a way to read רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון that could also fit רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מחלוקת of תנאים
Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test

steps.whatToRemember: רב says the thief who admits stays פטור, like the תנא קמא. שמואל says he is חייב when עדים come, like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. The גמרא now checks whether רב can also fit רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

phrases.english: According to Shmuel, it is certainly a dispute of tannaim;
according to Rav, shall we say it is a dispute of tannaim?

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁמוּאֵל וַדַּאי תַּנָּאֵי הִיא; לְרַב מִי לֵימָא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on שמואל's admission in step 13 and turns the question to רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב's ruling must depend on the מחלוקת of תנאים, or whether it could fit רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון too

steps.title: רב can fit even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב says his ruling works even for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. That תנא only obligates the thief when he admitted out of fear of the עדים. When a person admits on his own, even he agrees the thief is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can say: my ruling fits even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He only said the thief must pay in that case because the thief admitted out of fear of the witnesses. But here, where the person admits on his own, even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון agrees he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14. רב does not need to pick a side in the מחלוקת of the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the thief saw the עדים coming, so his admission was forced by fear. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says such a forced admission does not count. A real admission made freely, which is the case רב is talking about, still exempts from the קנס even according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Fear, being scared
On his own, by himself
He only said his ruling in this case and no further
Admits, or agrees (here it means agrees)

steps.whatToRemember: An admission made out of fear of the עדים is weaker than one made freely. So רב can fit both תנאים, while שמואל depends on רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.confusionAlert: The word מודה appears twice here with two meanings. First it means the thief 'admits'. At the end it means רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון 'agrees'.

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי – אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן;
phrases.english: What I said holds even according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon only said his ruling there
because the thief admits
out of fear of the witnesses;
but here, where he admits on his own,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה.
phrases.english: even Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon agrees.
phrases.notes: He agrees that the thief is exempt from the fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי – אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 by showing that רב's view fits both תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב also depend on the מחלוקת of the תנאים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון only obligates the thief when he admitted out of fear of the עדים. A free admission, which is רב's case, exempts according to everyone.

steps.title: רב המנונא: רב's rule works when the admission obligates the קרן
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says רב's rule makes sense when the thief says 'I stole' and then עדים come. He is פטור from the קנס, because his admission made him owe the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: רב's ruling makes sense where a person says 'I stole,' and then witnesses come and say he stole. He is exempt, because he obligated himself to pay the principal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא begins to define where רב's rule applies. This is the first half of his statement, and the next step gives the opposite case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The admission exempts from the קנס because it is a real admission that cost him something: he now owes the קרן. Since he made himself pay, his admission counts, and the later עדים cannot add a קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense
I stole
The principal, the value of what was stolen
He obligated himself (to pay)

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
Rav's statement makes sense
where someone says, 'I stole,'
and witnesses came saying that he stole: he is exempt,
phrases.notes: He is exempt from the fine, the double payment. He still pays back what he took.

phrases.english: since he obligated himself to pay the principal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב's view is established, רב המנונא narrows when it applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An admission exempts from the קנס when it makes the person owe at least the קרן.

steps.title: When the admission only tries to escape payment, he is חייב
steps.stepSummary: Take a thief who denied stealing, was proven a thief by עדים, and then admitted to slaughtering and selling before more עדים came. He is חייב in the fourfold or fivefold payment, because his admission did not make him owe anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: But suppose he said 'I did not steal,' and witnesses came saying he stole. Then he said 'I slaughtered and sold it,' and witnesses came saying he slaughtered and sold. He is liable, because his admission was only meant to get him out of paying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא finishes his statement with the opposite case, where רב's rule does not help the thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once עדים proved the theft, he already owed the קרן and כפל. His admission to slaughtering and selling added nothing he had to pay. It only tried to get him out of the fourfold or fivefold payment, so it does not count as an admission that exempts him.

keyTerms.meaning: I slaughtered and I sold (the stolen animal)
He exempted himself from everything (his admission cost him nothing)
Then he went on and said

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב המנונא, an admission only exempts from a קנס if it makes the person owe something. An admission that only gets him out of paying does not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a new requirement for רב's rule, and רבא attacks exactly this requirement in the next step.

phrases.english: But if he said, 'I did not steal,'
and witnesses came saying that he stole,
and then he said, 'I slaughtered and I sold it,'
and witnesses came saying that he slaughtered and sold it: he is liable,
phrases.notes: He is liable to pay four or five times the animal's value.

phrases.english: since he was exempting himself from everything.
phrases.notes: The theft was already proven by witnesses, so his admission didn't make him owe anything new. It only tried to get him out of paying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אָמַר ״לֹא גָּנַבְתִּי״, וּבָאוּ עֵדִים שֶׁגָּנַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of רב המנונא's statement, giving the opposite case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An admission that only exempts the person, and makes him owe nothing, does not stop the קנס when עדים come later.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב המנונא from רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he has beaten רב המנונא's argument. רבן גמליאל's admission only exempted him, yet רב חסדא used that case against רב הונא. רב הונא never answered that this case is different, so the distinction must be wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I have beaten the elders of the school of רב. In the story of רבן גמליאל, his admission was only exempting himself from everything. Yet רב חסדא used it against רב הונא, and רב הונא did not answer him with this difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב המנונא's distinction by pointing back to an earlier discussion between רב חסדא and רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב המנונא were right, רב הונא could easily have answered רב חסדא: 'The רבן גמליאל case is different, because his admission only exempted him.' Since רב הונא gave no such answer, רבא concludes that this distinction is not a real one.

keyTerms.meaning: I have beaten them, I got the better of them
The elders of the school of רב (here, רב המנונא)
He did not answer him (with this answer)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about רב's basic rule. He is only attacking רב המנונא's extra condition that the admission must make the person owe something.

phrases.english: Rava said:
I have beaten the elders of the school of Rav.
phrases.notes: He means רב המנונא and his distinction.

phrases.english: For Rabban Gamliel
was exempting himself from everything,
phrases.notes: This is the earlier story about רבן גמליאל and his slave. His admission didn't make him owe anything.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב הוּנָא –
phrases.english: and Rav Hisda said it to Rav Huna as a challenge,
and he did not answer him this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: קַפַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְסָבֵי דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction that רב המנונא made in steps 16 and 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב המנונא's distinction between an admission that obligates the קרן and one that only exempts the person.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב הונא never used this distinction to answer רב חסדא's challenge from רבן גמליאל, so the distinction does not seem to be accepted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the distinction were true, רב הונא would have used it to answer רב חסדא. His silence shows it was not accepted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן teaches the same distinction as רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also rules that a thief who admits and so makes himself owe the קרן is פטור from the קנס. But if he admits only after the theft was proven, his admission made him owe nothing, and he is חייב in the fourfold or fivefold payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a thief said 'I stole' and then עדים came, he is exempt, because he made himself owe the קרן. But if he said 'I did not steal,' עדים proved he stole, and then he said 'I slaughtered and sold,' and then עדים came for that, he is liable, because his admission made him owe nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יוחנן that says exactly what רב המנונא said. This backs up רב המנונא's distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 had רבא attacking רב המנונא's distinction. Now the גמרא shows that a major אמורא, רבי יוחנן, holds the very same distinction. The key test stays the same: did the admission make the thief owe money (exempt from the קנס), or did it only try to get him out of paying (still liable)?

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated; another אמורא taught the same idea
He made himself owe the original value
His admission only tried to get him out of paying; it made him owe nothing
I slaughtered and I sold, which is what triggers the fourfold or fivefold payment

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he said "I stole," and then witnesses came that he stole,
he is exempt, since he made himself owe the principal.
But if he said "I did not steal,"
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, making it "I did not steal."

phrases.english: and witnesses came that he stole,
and then he said, "I slaughtered and sold it,"
and then witnesses came that he slaughtered and sold it,
he is liable, since he was only trying to free himself from paying anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 18 indirectly by showing that רבי יוחנן holds רב המנונא's distinction.
steps.raayaObject: רב המנונא's distinction between an admission that makes the thief owe something and one that frees him from paying
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of רבי יוחנן, passed on by רבי חייא בר אבא

steps.title: רב אשי brings support from the wording of a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says a משנה and a ברייתא are both worded in line with this distinction. He quotes the משנה: if the theft was proven by two עדים, and the slaughter or sale only by one עד or his own admission, he pays double but not four or five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the משנה and a ברייתא are both precise in this way. The משנה says: if he stole according to two witnesses, and slaughtered and sold according to one witness or by his own word, he pays double but does not pay four or five.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי announces that the wording of a משנה and a ברייתא supports רב המנונא and רבי יוחנן. First he quotes the משנה, setting up a close reading of it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב אשי only quotes the משנה; the proof itself comes from a careful look at its wording. The case: the theft is proven by two עדים, so he owes double. The slaughter or sale is not properly proven, so he does not owe four or five.

keyTerms.meaning: It is precise; its exact wording proves a point
A teaching of the תנאים left out of the משנה
Double payment owed by a thief
By his own admission

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
A mishnah and a baraita are also precise this way.
The mishnah, as we learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on the previous page, ע״ד ב.

phrases.english: If he stole, according to two witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: וְטָבַח וּמָכַר עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: and slaughtered or sold, according to one witness
or by his own admission,
he pays the double payment,
but he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַתְנִיתִין וּבָרַיְיתָא נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second line of support, this time from the wording of a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction of רב המנונא and רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה on ע״ד ב (and later a ברייתא)

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention two witnesses for the theft?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks why the משנה says the theft was proven by two עדים. It could have taught a simpler case: theft and slaughter both by one עד or his own admission, where he pays only the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to say 'he stole according to two witnesses'? Let it say: he stole and slaughtered and sold according to one witness or his own admission, and he pays only the principal!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי points out that the משנה's wording seems to include an extra, unneeded detail. He is setting up the lesson he will draw from that detail, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה only wanted to teach that one עד or an admission cannot create a קנס, a simpler case would have done the job. Since the משנה made a point of saying the theft was proven by two עדים, that detail must be teaching something. רב אשי will use it to support the distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks why a detail is included)
Let it teach; suggests a simpler wording
He pays only the original value, with no fine

phrases.english: Why do I need it to teach
"he stole, according to two witnesses"?
Let it teach: he stole and slaughtered [or sold]
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד אוֹ עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ –
phrases.english: according to one witness or by his own admission,
and he pays only the principal!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי דְּתָנֵי גָּנַב עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the משנה just quoted to begin drawing the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה chose a case where the theft was proven by two עדים instead of a simpler case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer comes on the next amud.
